subject: Recap: Clarion Health — private/VPC constraints, residency & next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@clarionhealth.com>, Olivia Price <olivia.price@clarionhealth.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Clarion Health — private/VPC constraints, residency & next steps

Thanks again for the time today — good discussion. Quick recap of what I captured and the proposed next steps so we can align internally and with your network/security team.

Top pain points you called out:
- Data residency: all PHI must remain within US East region (no cross-region replication).
- Regulatory/air-gap requirement: certain state contracts require no persistent outbound internet for PHI processing; this may force an on-prem air-gapped or VPC with controlled egress model.
- Key management: customer-managed keys (AWS KMS CMK) or HSM support is mandatory for some datasets.
- Network posture: no NAT egress except to pre-approved hosts; strict IP allowlisting; TLS inspection currently is not allowed for PHI traffic.
- Auditability: 7-year retention of access/audit logs and a certification of secure deletion on termination.

Clarified goals:
- Pilot a scoped workload (redacted data set) in Q4 for 6 weeks to validate latency, cost, and audit controls.
- Goal: production decision by end of Q1 FY27.

Immediate asks / action items we agreed:
1) Clarion -> share the internal network diagram + explicit list of outbound egress requirements (attached: clarion-internal-network.png).
2) Clarion -> confirm legal's exact CMK/HSM requirements and whether an on-prem HSM is preferred or an AWS KMS CMK with an external HSM is acceptable.
3) Redwood -> scope a Private/VPC configuration (options: VPC peering w/ private endpoints vs dedicated on-prem nodes) and provide an initial cost/time estimate.
4) Schedule a 60-minute design workshop with your NetSec and infra leads (Sergio will lead from our side).
5) Procurement: Marissa will prep a draft SOW and we’ll route it to procurement@clarionhealth.com for review.

Attachments: clarion-network-constraints.pdf (you shared this during call), MAP-clarion.xlsx (mutual action plan template).

Proposed next meeting: Wed Sep 1, 10:00–11:00 AM ET — confirm availability.

If I missed anything or misstated a requirement, please flag. Otherwise, we’ll start preparing the SOW + technical pre-work.

—
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions Sales | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Samir Rao <samir@clarionhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Price <olivia.price@clarionhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Clarion Health — private/VPC constraints, residency & next steps

Jonas — thanks for the tidy recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Legal requires encryption at rest with customer-managed keys; our preference today is an AWS KMS CMK backed by an on-prem HSM for key escrow. Please confirm Redwood supports external KMS integrations and the option for HSM-backed keys.
- The "no persistent outbound internet" requirement applies to any environment processing PHI for State X contracts. We are evaluating two paths: a) VPC with egress strictly to Redwood-managed IP ranges via a dedicated AWS Transit Gateway and no other internet egress, or b) fully air-gapped on-prem instance that only accepts model updates via signed artifacts and physical transfer.
- Audit & retention: we need a statement of compliance for 7-year retention and deletion certification when the service is decommissioned.

I attached our internal network diagram (clarion-internal-network.png). Procurement is tracking on our side — I looped them (procurement@clarionhealth.com). We can do the design workshop on Wed Sep 1, 10–11 AM ET, that works for NetSec and infra.

– Samir Rao
Head of Data Platforms, Clarion Health
samir@clarionhealth.com | +1 (617) 555-1620

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@clarionhealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Clarion Health — private/VPC constraints, residency & next steps

Thanks Samir/Jonas — adding some technical notes ahead of the design workshop so we can use them as pre-work.

Networking and connectivity considerations we recommend you confirm with NetSec: 
- Preferred model: VPC with AWS PrivateLink endpoints to a dedicated Redwood private control plane in us-east-1. PrivateLink removes public internet egress; all traffic flows over the AWS network.
- If PrivateLink is not an option, we can support strict egress via a Transit Gateway and IP allowlist. We will provide a list of FQDNs and IP ranges to allow; these are stable for a dedicated private deployment.
- Ports: outbound 443 required to our endpoints; additional outbound ports may be required for telemetry and health checks but can be routed to a telemetry proxy.
- CMK/HSM: we support AWS KMS CMKs and integration points for customer key material. For air-gapped on-prem installs, we can consume signed model artifacts and support offline updates via provided tooling (signed tarball + manifest).
- Audit logs: we can export detailed access logs to your S3 (locked bucket) or to an on-prem SIEM. Retention policies can be configured to meet 7-year requirements; we will include a deletion certification clause in the SOW.

Pre-work for the workshop (please send before Fri Aug 29):
1) Finalized network diagram and egress policy (you already shared a draft — thanks).
2) NetSec contact + certificate authority (if you're using internal PKI).
3) Clarification on whether TLS interception (for DLP) will be permitted for non-PHI traffic; full TLS interception for PHI is a no-go.

I’ll pull together a pilot topology doc and a rough cost estimate for PrivateLink + 2 dedicated GPU nodes for the pilot (ballpark) and share it in advance.

Cheers,
Sergio
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
